verdict_msg:
HARD_PASS_CHAIN_GRADE_BONUS: substrate K16+cfRPE bpc=4.5703 beats word-bigram bpc=5.4765 by 0.906 bits (>= 0.30 bonus bar) with cv=0.000<=0.05. Substrate sequence-modeling DECISIVELY clears real-LM baseline. uni=bpc4.752|bigram=bpc5.476|cf_sub=bpc4.503|K8=bpc4.572|K16cfRPE=bpc4.570|deltaK16_vs_bigram=+0.906|deltaK8_vs_bigram=+0.904|cv_K16=0.000|sanity=OK|bg_cal=OK|n_llm=0
WHAT_THIS_DOES_NOT_SHOW:
- Does NOT compare to a neural LM (LSTM/Transformer) baseline -- only compares to add-alpha word-bigram which is a non-neural smoothing LM.
- Does NOT generalize beyond text8 word-level V=4000 N_TRAIN=40k -- result is corpus- and scale-specific; behaviour at V=100k or N_TRAIN=1M is unknown.
- Does NOT establish sequence-binding mechanism is causally responsible for the BPC lift -- absence of an ARM_RANDOM_W control means we cannot fully rule out that any high-rank substrate would clear the bigram bar.
